description: This Harvard Dataverse collection contains a household survey of 322 arable-farming households in four subcounties of Nwoya district, northern Uganda. Researchers gathered responses during 1–21 December 2017 to examine food security, nutrition, agricultural shocks and uptake of climate-smart agriculture. The public inventory lists a questionnaire, codebook and paired tabular files for survey modules covering household circumstances, market access, expenditure and food scarcity. The named repository API returned unrestricted files and explicit CC BY 4.0 terms; its HTML landing returned HTTP 202 in this environment. This is a district sample, not a national census or an observed food-transport network. Questionnaire responses and derived resilience interpretations may depend on household recall and study definitions. A reviewer-assessed use is constructing household decisions or stress scenarios for food-supply simulations. platform-global-food-twin is related by food-system purpose, but no data interface or direct adoption is established. The article names a separate GitHub companion that currently returns HTTP 404; it is not the verified access route. No respondent file was downloaded.
